title: Analysis: Lula presidency saved at least 20,000km2 of Brazilian Amazon since 2022 - Carbon Brief
gist: Carbon Brief estimates Lula's presidency avoided at least 20,000km2 of Amazon deforestation versus a no-forest-code-enforcement (Bolsonaro proxy) scenario, with annual loss more than halving from 11,594km2 (2022) to 5,731km2 (2025) and 2026 possibly a record low. The neck-and-neck October 2026 election against Flávio Bolsonaro, the collapse of the soy moratorium and a right-leaning congress make future Amazon deforestation highly politically contingent.

insights.claim: Annual Amazon deforestation in Brazil more than halved from 11,594 km2 in 2022 to 5,731 km2 in 2025 after Lula replaced Bolsonaro.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Shows enforcement policy moves forest-loss rates fast, material for deforestation-linked supply chains and carbon/forest finance.
